startup.name: Standard Gaussian
startup.description: Three person San Francisco team in Spring 2026 building world models for finance. The input gives no description, so whether the product is a learned market simulator, a forecasting model, a research tool for funds or a trading business is unknown, as are the founders backgrounds and any customers.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent range). Up for a technical team, an AI finance theme that matches recent YC interest, and likely quant pedigree implied by the name. Down because the input has no description and no traction, and similar quant lab companies in comps show little progress. Net about 3 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say that a world model for finance is a research ambition with no customer or evidence of edge, and that a three person team without a verified result looks like many quant AI pitches. Without a clear buyer, partners may prefer a more specific product.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is only 7.4 months from 2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchor 0.57 ever for Fintech; with a median of 6 to 7 months from batch start to seed, about half of eventual seeds close inside 7.4 months, giving 0.29, and 0.30 is 0.53x of the anchor because of the short window and not a judgment on the team. The hot AI finance theme is not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, for a three person research team raising quickly.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later YC median of 4.1M.
Strong seed for a research heavy AI finance team, since press covered AI seeds run above the median.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if the pitch of world models for finance stays a research claim with no backtest or paying fund inside seven months. Quant research startups such as Zoa Research, Event Horizon Labs and Sharpe have shown no public round years after YC, and funds guard data and results. Investors may also wait for a result before pricing a three person lab.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C in seven months would require a foundation model scale outcome, as for the largest AI labs only. outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company proves nothing beyond a backtest and stalls, the usual path of quant research startups, or the team joins a fund. The upside would come if the model shows real predictive edge and a fund or the team trades it, a rare event with large rewards for a very small share of such labs.

technical_complexity.rationale: Learned world models of markets face noisy, non stationary data and little ground truth, and compute and data costs are high. A small team can run experiments in months but proving an edge is the hard open problem. If solved it is the moat; the input does not show progress.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large quant firms and AI labs could build similar models, but they gain nothing by selling them, so copying is likelier internal than as a competing product.

narrative.general_summary: Standard Gaussian is a three person Spring 2026 team building world models for finance, with no description or traction in the input. The window is just 7.4 months from 2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17, so only about half of eventual seeds fall inside it, giving 0.30 against a Fintech anchor of 0.57 for ever. Series A given seed is 0.03 because Fintech Series A medians are over two years from batch start. Quant AI peers in comps show few public rounds. The odds do not rank this company against others.
